subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — laddered H100/A100/L4 phasing for StratifyAI
messages:
From: Chris Novak <chris@stratify.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Ops Team <ops@stratify.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — mission-critical inference + bursty peaks

Hi Priyom,

Quick intro: we're close to signature on a 12-month Dedicated commitment but need help nailing the initial SKU mix. Our workload is a mix of short-response chat + episodic multi-turn summarization jobs that spike during business hours and at known weekly batch windows. Latency requirements: 95th < 350ms for chat; batch can be lower. Memory per model: we have two families — a 70B quantized for chat and a 180B fine-tuned summarizer.

We asked our infra team to run rough perf numbers (attached) but could use Redwood's guidance on a laddered approach (start with one SKU, add others as committed volume grows). Key constraints: cost predictability for procurement, the need for graceful degradation if dedicated capacity is saturated, and short warm-up for KV cache on model variants.

Can you propose an initial mix (H100/A100/L4), a phasing plan tied to committed CU thresholds, and fallback behavior when H100s are occupied? We're ok with a hybrid of reserved + burst.

Appreciate it — Chris
StratifyAI — Head of Platform

Attachment: stratify_perf_snapshot.csv (csv)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Chris Novak <chris@stratify.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — mission-critical inference + bursty peaks

Chris — thanks for the context and the perf snapshot. High level recommendation in short: laddered capacity that prioritizes H100 for the 180B summarizer (memory + perf), A100 as balanced workhorse for 70B chat at scale, and L4 for low-cost, high-concurrency chat tail/embedding-style requests.

Summary proposal (full attached workbook contains per-token cost and utilization math):
- Phase 0 (contract signing, baseline): 4x H100 (80GB), 8x A100 (80GB slot equivalents), 12x L4 (48GB) for initial steady-state. This supports peak-preserving capacity for the summarizer and provides headroom for chat.
- Phase 1 (at 40% committed CU growth): add +4 A100, +8 L4. Start redirecting non-critical long-context chat to L4 variants trimmed/quantized for memory.
- Phase 2 (at 80% CU growth or sustained 95th P50 latency degradation): spin up additional 4 H100s and convert 2 A100 slots to reserve H100-only queue for the summarizer's batch windows.

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Memory vs perf: 180B summarizer needs H100-class memory (80GB) to avoid aggressive offloading. A100 80GB may be feasible with ZeRO partitioning but adds latency and operational complexity. L4 (48GB) is unsuitable for the full 180B but excellent for trimmed-chat and reranks.
- Cost hedging: recommend conservative reserved H100 count for baseline summarizer SLOs, and use burst A100 on reserved or marketplace pools for chat spikes. L4 reserved slots provide cheap concurrency cushion.
- Fallback: when H100 pool saturated, automatically route summarizer batch windows to staggered A100 heavy-slot pools with a short degraded-SLO label (e.g., 2x latency target). Redwood's smart routing can enforce canary runs for 1-2% of requests to validate A100 behavior before broad fallback.
- KV cache: reserve warm nodes for summarizer to keep KV residency; warm-up cost is non-trivial so avoid immediate fallback for sustained windows — prefer pre-allocated standby H100s or prewarmed A100s during scheduled batch runs.

I'll attach the sizing workbook and a short runbook for laddered phasing. Internal ops and product folks — see callouts inline, we should validate node packing and NUMA constraints with ops.

Next step: propose a 30-minute call to walk the matrix and align on procurement triggers.

—Priyom
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachment: stratify_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (xlsx), laddering-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — laddered H100/A100/L4 phasing for StratifyAI

Quick internal notes on ops implications before we present to Chris: 

1) Node packing & NUMA: H100 SXM pods are best for the 180B. If they require multi-card model sharding, we need to reserve whole pods rather than slice slots; that affects the effective slot count. Add a column in the workbook for "pod-occupancy factor".

2) Prewarm strategy: For scheduled batch windows (they mentioned weekly jobs) we should offer a scheduled prewarm API that the customer can trigger 30–60 minutes in advance so caches and CUDA kernels are hot. That reduces cold-start latency more than just standby nodes.

3) Price modeling: If Stratify wants procurement predictability, give them a hybrid contract: reserved H100 baseline (monthly commit), reserved L4 baseline for concurrency, and a small percentage of committed A100 that acts as burst tokens. That framing makes it easier for finance to forecast.

4) Fallback automation: I'll add an automatic roll-forward test that runs a short 5–10 minute load test on A100 fallback during lower traffic windows to ensure that their long-context summarizer doesn't regress badly.

I'll sync the updated workbook and a simple slide for procurement. LMK if I should call them directly or you want to run the joint call.

—Dev
Sr. Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Chris Novak <chris@stratify.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated laddered SKU plan & next steps (StratifyAI)

Chris — thanks for the chat earlier. Attached is the workbook and a short runbook that captures the phased SKU laddering, procurement triggers, and ops playbook. TL;DR: the recommended conservative baseline keeps 4 H100 to guarantee summarizer SLOs, with A100 and L4 used to scale chat and provide cost-efficient concurrency.

Actionables:
- We propose the following procurement trigger points (mutual action plan):
  * Sign + baseline provisioning (4 H100 / 8 A100 / 12 L4) — Redwood will reserve these within 5 business days of contract effective date.
  * 40% committed CU increase — automatic order for +4 A100 / +8 L4 (approx. 30–45 day lead time).
  * 80% and sustained latency distress — escalate to add +4 H100 (requires 60–90 day lead time for reserved procurement).

- Ops: we will provide a scheduled prewarm endpoint and a pre-authorized fallback policy that routes summarizer batch windows to A100 with an explicit degraded-SLO flag. We recommend a 2-week test window during the evaluation period where Redwood will run fallback regression tests nightly.

Please confirm and we can put the MAP into DocuSign with these triggers and attach the workbook. Happy to walk through the workbook live — how does Friday 10:00 PT look for a 30-minute call?

Thanks,
—Priyom
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
